steps.text: To assemble the sandwiches: Layer ham, Brie cheese, apricot preserves, and mustard in equal amounts on two pieces of bread, topping with the remaining two slices of bread. Brush top of each sandwich with olive oil.

Heat a grill pan over medium heat. Once the pan is hot, place sandwiches, oiled-side down, in the pan. Brush top of each sandwich with oil. Cook each side until bread is golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Brie Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: Black forest ham, brie, Dijon mustard, and apricot preserves are grilled on Italian bread to make these delightfully simple sandwiches that go beyond a typical grilled cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Ham and Brie Sandwich

review.reviewBody: Good sandwich but prefer to use mango chutney (a tangy one) in place of apricot preserves. The apricot was too sweet for our tastes. I am sure other meats could replace the ham, e.g. turkey, chicken.

This was awesome! I will definitely make it again. I made it with sliced open faced baguettes. Pre toasted the bread first. Then layered the slices with the Brie some orange marmalade and then thin sliced Black Forest ham put it back in the oven at 350 to melt the cheese. Wow! It took about 5 or 6 minutes to melt. I forgot the mustard.

These were amazing. I made them on large croissants from Sam's Club, slathered jelly on both sides rolled up 4 pieces of Black Forest Ham and a large chunk of the brie in the middle with a generous dollop of dijon then popped them in the oven for about 5 minutes on 375 degrees, just enough to melt the brie and make the croissant crisp. Easy for a large crowd. We did trays of 15 and served fifty. They were a real hit.

Mmmmmm! Cut back a little on the mustard. Also really good with raspberry preserves if no apricot in the house. If raspberry seeds are an issue for you, use seedless raspberry jam. For anybody with difficulty getting the brie to melt on the sandwich, heat your ham slices in a hot pan for just a few seconds to heat it up before layering the brie onto it.

made it on rye bread. Used saucy susan for apricot 
preserves. Used spicy brown mustard. Used a good quality brie which was very hard to work with. cooked with olive oil. Tasted great! Will make again.

Saw this in the Allrecipes magazine and thought what a good idea for a simple dinner, especially since I hadn't grilled sandwiches in quite awhile. The magazine says any jam will work, but I did use apricot and loved it. I also used a different cheese, I think an Irish cheddar, and that provided excellent flavor. In honor of Autumn, I paired the sandwiches with an easy homemade pumpkin soup. A great dinner!
Perfect as is. This is the recipe I chose to use to break in my new panini machine and it made me so happy I bought it! I used a ciabatta loaf from Trader Joe’s and it worked perfectly...

I made this as a late Friday evening supper. I chose it simply due to the fact that it did not have a 1/4 - 1/2 cup of butter as the others did. It is awesome. Yummmm. I made a few modifications based upon what was already in fridge. Used orange marmalade and spicy brown mustard :>. Also sprinkled just a bit of garlic on one slice of bread...what's a recipe without garlic. Came out wonderful. Now my husband gives this 4 star as he felt the orange marmalade was a bit too sweet. But the recipe didn't call for orange marmalade! I tried to find the mango chutney at a local grocery store to no avail. I think next time I will just cut the amount of jam in half as it was really a nice complement to the brie. We also needed to zap in microwave for 30 secs...didn't get hot enough. This made perfect. Make sure your brie gets nice and hot and slightly runny. Makes perfect.

This is awesome! I used peach jelly (it was all we had). The flavors of the jelly and the mustard complement each other really well. I would use thick cut ham in future as we used the thin shaved ham and the flavor was not strong enough

Served a group of 20 lunch today... most knew there was something different about these sandwiches ... everyone loved them... no one guessed sugar free apricot preserves which is so good with the Brie Cheese... I used French bread and grilled them in the Panini press. Big Hit!

This was a really good sandwich, boys loved it. We used jalapeno jelly instead of apricot preserves. Just regular bread. We also added a fried egg.

I'm not eating carbs so I ate without the bread and still very good.

Perfect on all measurements and instructions. I used Farmer John ham due to cost. But my change of bread made a big impact -- subbed vague "Italian bread" with circular Naan bread, available at the grocery. It grilled up perfectly and it was the ideal size for such a rich sandwich.

This was a hit! My family loved it. I accidentally picked up a package of turkey instead of ham in the deli section and it still worked great. For our girls I put less Dijon as they are not fond of spicy hot as much. This recipe is a keeper

Really enjoyed this. It's a strange pairing of ingredients, but it really works. An easy, make at home gourmet sandwich. I plan to experiment with other cheeses. I recommend going easy on the apricot spread. I misread and put way too much on for my first try, but it was still delicious.
Loved it! this is a winner! and the Husband loved it! will use this one again. Great job!
Great Sandwich. Loved it. So did my husband! It’s a keeper!

Very delicious sandwich. I used thickly sliced italian bread and used my indoor countertop grill that has a lid to grill the sandwich. Next time, I'll omit the mustard on mine and add more preserves. My husband said omit the preserves and add more mustard! It was really very good
My kids saw me making these and what went in them and said yuck! Then they loved them and asked for more! These were a hit all around! Easy too and quick. Perfect for school night.
We made this for dinner and served it with grapes. It was delicious! The apricot preserves added a sweet flavor to the sandwich. We will definately make it again!
This looked like a gourmet sandwich but was so easy to make. Loved the tangy apricot preserves with the Brie. I will make again.
